basis: Intellectual disability, pyloric stenosis and cranial skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; craniosynostosis occurs in 30–79%; cryptorchidism is outside the axes.
GnRH deficiency with defining Kallmann-spectrum olfactory dysfunction; hearing abnormalities and bone loss lack established common direct involvement.
Inherited generalized epilepsy with febrile and afebrile seizures; no established extra-neurologic involvement.
An inherited erythrocyte membrane permeability disorder; the affected cells are red blood cells.
Benign tumour arising in the nasopharynx, which belongs to the upper respiratory tract.
A glioblastoma variant arising in brain tissue.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, tremor and ataxia; reported manifestations are neurologic.
Infiltrative fibroblastic neoplasm of soft connective tissues and fascia; subtype-specific locations do not establish additional axes across the group.
Histiocytic neoplasm with skin, liver and skeletal infiltration as defining multisystem manifestations; lung and CNS involvement are less consistent.
Localized benign cutaneous foam-cell lesion; despite its xanthoma ancestry, it does not establish a systemic lipid disorder.
Defining subcutaneous fat loss and insulin-resistant dysmetabolism; steatosis occurs in 5–29%; hypertension and atherosclerosis are separately diagnosed complications.
Acute inflammatory, typically immune-mediated optic neuropathy; the optic nerve is assigned to the ocular axis.
Familial infantile myeloid leukemia-like disorder affecting blood and marrow; no common direct extra-haematologic damage established.
Inherited sideroblastic anemia with reported thrombocytopenia and neutropenia; all established abnormalities affect blood-cell production.
Cyclic immune-mediated eosinophilia with defining cutaneous angioedema; transient swelling does not support additional involvement; visceral injury is atypical.
Renal agenesis/dysplasia and vertebral segmentation defects define MURCS; reproductive malformations have no axis; hearing impairment occurs in 5–29%.
NMJ disease; myopathy and ptosis/ophthalmoparesis each occur in 30–79%, with muscle atrophy reported; respiratory and swallowing weakness do not establish lung or gut injury.
Microbial biofilm-associated inflammation destroys tooth-supporting periodontal tissues; teeth and gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Chronic pancreatic inflammation and fibrosis damage the exocrine pancreas; secondary diabetes is separately diagnosed, so no additional endocrine label.
Severe neonatal skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae and metaphyses; the SBDS association alone does not establish marrow or pancreatic involvement.
Acute adrenal steroid failure; hypotension and prerenal dysfunction do not establish direct vascular or renal injury; autoimmune etiology is not universal.
Congenital atrial septal malformation with left-to-right shunting; dyspnea does not establish lung injury, and stroke is very rare.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; renal hypoplasia and exocrine pancreatic insufficiency each reported in 1/3 patients; small samples limit certainty; hepatomegaly alone excluded.
Malignant adipose-tissue tumour arising in the skin.
Clonal marrow disorder with ineffective hematopoiesis and sideroblastic anemia; hepatic findings are occasional and heart failure very rare.
